subject: biology
title: Golgi Apparatus
summary: The Golgi apparatus is the cell's sorting and shipping center - a stack of flattened membrane pouches that finishes, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids, then sends them off in bubbles to where they are needed.

compareCandidate.label: ER vs. Golgi
compareCandidate.description: The ER is the workshop where proteins and fats are built. The Golgi is the sorting and shipping center that finishes, labels, and dispatches them.

processes: Receiving proteins and lipids from the ER
plainLanguageExplanation: The Golgi apparatus looks like a stack of flattened pancakes or a delivery depot. It receives proteins and lipids from the ER in transport bubbles, then sorts and packages them for their next destination. It may tag them with labels that say where they belong, or wrap them in new membrane bubbles. Some products are shipped out of the cell entirely. In this way the Golgi is the cell's mailroom: receiving, finishing, addressing, and dispatching.

whyItMatters: The Golgi decides where everything the cell makes should go. Without it, proteins and fats would pile up unsorted and the cell could not deliver its products to the right places.
didYouKnow: Every minute, thousands of tiny bubbles arrive at the Golgi and leave from it, like a very busy loading dock.
